design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (respite_and_trial_stays). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,5,5]; respite_ext_advance_payment took 6, respite_ext_returned_payment_fee 5, respite_ext_medication_setup 5.

WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller (financial POA) only wants to pay what is due so her mother's booked stay can begin on 2026-11-02, by debit card. The advance policy states 'The advance is fixed only after the stay's records carry a returned-payment fee for every returned payment on the stay.' and 'The advance is not worked out until the stay carries its medication setup charge whenever the stay type includes medication administration and the physician's report is on file.' The ledger shows the 1673.00 ACH return of 2026-10-27 with no fee, and the stay shows a physician's report dated 2026-10-24 on a stay type with medication administration but no setup charge. The agent must find both from the records, post them with their own multi-factor amounts, then hand over the payment with the advance computed from the stay, its ledger, the independent living account and the Entrance Fee Agreement.

SCOPE. Task 0 occupied the level-change credit, the level-change segment and the signed extension with their three tools; task 1 claims respite_ext_returned_payment_fee, respite_ext_medication_setup, respite_ext_advance_payment and post_returned_payment_fee_57d4cb7a, post_medication_setup_fee_0971281c, pay_stay_advance_b4214d09. Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies with disjoint scopes.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root respite_ext_advance_payment (pay_stay_advance_b4214d09, owner=user). Edge A: advance -> returned_payment_fee, value_input, gate fees_returned, form state, affirmative sentence above; only post_returned_payment_fee_57d4cb7a writes returned_payment add-ons; false at opening: respite_ledger.833c7671 is a respite_payment_return and the ledger has no add-on. Edge B: advance -> medication_setup, value_input, gate fees_setup, form state, negated sentence above; only post_medication_setup_fee_0971281c writes medication_setup add-ons; false at opening: respite_stays.da9d5495 health_documents_date 2026-10-24, Standard Care includes medication administration, no medication_setup add-on. Fan-out; the two writes commute (verified by replaying setup-then-fee: identical 78.46, 92.76, 3994.72 and balance 4790.22). Deletion runs: without the fee the advance is 3916.26; without the setup it is 3901.96. user_scenario mentions only the bank's returned-payment email and the wish to pay; it names no fee or setup charge. Tools check nothing.

FACTOR CARD.
returned_payment_fee (78.46; baseline 35.00): statutory_service_charge method (Harbor View, Florida tiered: 1673.00 -> greater of 40 and 5% = 83.65) -> 45.62 at baseline; resident_first_return_courtesy 25% (independent_ledger return 05a8ee8d 2026-05-06, one in twelve months) -> 97.29; life_plan_return_courtesy 10% (occupied LifeChoice 50% Refundable Plan) -> 84.74; bank_return_item_charge 12.00 (latest payment ACH) -> 66.46; pre_arrival_handling 10.00 (6 days before arrival) -> 68.46.
medication_setup (92.76; baseline 85.00): packaging_method 2 fourteen-night cycles x 60 = 120.00 -> 70.08; life_plan_setup_discount 10% -> 101.40; pharmacy_profile_reduction 20% (43 months) -> 112.20; early_booking_reduction 10% (21-day lead) -> 101.40; rush_packaging 15.00 (report 9 days before arrival) -> 77.76.
advance_payment (3994.72; baseline 1444.22 = 7 x 239 + 171.22 - 400): advance_nights 21 -> 1445.72; receipts_counted good funds only (0 vs 400.00) -> 3594.72; life_plan_advance_relief 10% -> 4419.55; residency_deferral 10% -> 4419.55; early_booking_relief 5% -> 4195.96; account_standing_relief 1% -> 4033.34. Multi-source (conditions over distinct records): advance_nights (stay return rows AND stay dates / independent ledger), account_standing_relief (independent balance AND independent ledger returns), resident_first_return_courtesy (residency row AND independent ledger); the plan factors' conjunctions read one agreement row. Cross-difficulty: independent residency ed3a5415 with ledger rows (return 05a8ee8d inside the twelve-month window), entrance agreement cc46750c. Near-miss: the 400.00 ACH payment is a real, cleared receipt that the standard method counts but the returned-payment method excludes; the May 2026 independent return is inside the twelve-month window while the October autopay is good.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Returned fee and setup (respite_addon_charge): respite_addons has no structured eligibility - posted against the stay in any status. Advance (respite_payment): respite_prepayment_and_check_in and respite_payments_and_refunds have no gate on payments; the stay is booked and payments may be posted while booked. No time gate applies; the prepayment deadline (arrival 2026-11-02 less 3 days = 2026-10-30) is still ahead at frozen 2026-10-29. Overwrites declared: the returned-payment fee clause, the medication setup clause, and the minimum-stay-in-advance sentence.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Stay da9d5495; return 833c7671 references payment 9889b71c; the 400.00 payment da224820 is not returned; the independent living fee charges, payments, return and its 35.00 fee belong to residency ed3a5415 and only feed tier conditions.

SEED. Customer e1cf21ee (Ruth Okafor, rep Grace Okafor financial_poa 9195550188). Stay balance 4619.00 = 5019 - 400 - 1673 + 1673. Independent living balance 0.00 = (September 2025: 4529.36 - 4529.36 + 4529.36 + 35 - 4564.36) + (May 2026: 4529.36 - 4529.36 + 4529.36 + 35 - 4564.36) + (October 2026: 4529.36 - 4529.36). No automatic clause fires: the stay is booked before its arrival, no cancellation, no check-in due. Paying by debit card carries no convenience fee (base charges it on credit card payments only), so the root write ignites no further obligation.

PERSONA. Grace is organised and brief; volunteers only the bounced payment email and the wish to pay today by debit card; gives DOB 1946-07-22 and SSN 6047 only when asked; agrees if told charges must be put on the account first; pays the figure given with her debit card; ends after confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read stay, ledger, independent residency, independent ledger, Entrance Fee Agreement; post returned-payment fee 78.46 referencing 833c7671; post medication setup 92.76; hand over the payment: debit_card, 3994.72. _verify.py (authoring-only, removed) replays gold with the real tools; check_compute recomputes 78.46, 92.76, 3994.72.

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules and records: both state sentences are unmet; the community, the returned amount, the independent ledger, the plan, the dates and the payment instruments each select one tier; the debit card is the only instrument the caller offers that the returned-payment receipts method counts. One solution found.

ROUND 2 (audit audits/policy_task/respite_and_trial_stays round 1).
T1-F1 (no near-miss in the returned-payment fee and the medication setup) -> seeded an independent living return outside the twelve-month window (2025-09-01 fee be4e7330, autopay 334f9091 returned e0db33a3 on 2025-09-12 with its 35.00 fee 624b80c5, cured by cashier's check 46aa83f4; account still 0.00) and a rescinded LifeCare Declining Balance Plan agreement edc2cbd3 (signed 2022-08-15, rescission notice 2022-08-19 = day 4 of Harbor View's 7-day rescission period counted from the signing date as day 0, 100 percent refund due by 2022-09-18 and paid, closed 2022-09-12; then the occupied LifeChoice 50% plan was signed 2022-11-02). A reader counting the 2025 return gets a 0 percent courtesy (fee 97.29); a reader taking the rescinded LifeCare plan gets a 25 percent courtesy (69.05), a zero packaging charge (setup 15.00) and a 25 percent advance relief. The rules read only returns 'in the last twelve months' and an 'occupied' agreement, so all scored values are unchanged (78.46 / 92.76 / 3994.72). The cross reads with status filters already exclude the rescinded agreement; XCOUNT within twelve months excludes the 2025 return.
O-T1-1: the gate recomputes factor_sensitivity with Python float rounding, so statutory_service_charge stays 45.62 (exact half-up of 45.625 would be 45.63); the factor bears weight either way. O-T1-2 multi-source claim corrected above.

ROUND 3 (audit revision_2). T1-R2-F1: the rescinded LifeCare agreement edc2cbd3 now carries a rescission notice dated 2022-08-19, day 4 of the Harbor View rescission period (7 days, signing date 2022-08-15 as day 0), with the rescission refund due 2022-09-18 (30 days) and the agreement closed 2022-09-12; a rescission is reachable under the entrance charter. It is still not occupied, so it remains the near-miss for the three Life Plan factors and no scored value moves (78.46 / 92.76 / 3994.72). O-T1-R2-1: the SEED card's independent balance now lists the September 2025 rows.
user_scenario:
You are Grace Okafor, the daughter of Ruth Okafor, and you hold her financial power of attorney. Your mother lives in her own independent living apartment at Larkspur at Harbor View in Sarasota, and she is booked into a short assisted living respite stay on the same campus starting Monday, November 2, while you are away for work. This morning your bank emailed you that the payment you sent last week toward that stay was returned - you had switched checking accounts and forgot the old one was closing. You are calling to pay whatever has to be paid now so that your mother can still arrive on Monday, and you want to pay it yourself, today, with your debit card; you do not want anything taken from a bank account again. You are organised and a little embarrassed about the bounced payment, and you get to the point quickly.
When asked whose account this is, you give your name and your mother's full name, Ruth Okafor. Only when the agent asks to verify do you give her date of birth, 1946-07-22, and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 6047; if a phone number is wanted, hers is 9195550163 and yours is 9195550188. You do not remember the exact amounts already paid, you have no reference numbers, and you say so if asked.
If the agent explains that some charges have to be put on her stay account before the amount due can be given, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you how much is due, you accept the figure. When the agent hands the payment over to you, you pay that amount with your debit card using exactly the details the agent gives you. Once the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them and end the call without raising anything else.
